about.title: Redlands Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Five people died in traffic collisions in Redlands during 2025, according to public records. Behind each of those numbers is a household in San Bernardino County that suddenly had to think about funeral arrangements, a missing paycheck, and an empty chair at the table. A wrongful death claim exists for those families. It is a civil action, separate from any criminal case prosecutors may bring, and it asks whether someone's negligence caused the loss. In Redlands, many of these losses trace back to collisions along the I-10, Orange Street, Alabama Street, and Lugonia Avenue, though a claim can also arise from an unsafe property, a defective product, or medical care that fell short. California law gives eligible family members two years from the date of death to file, and that window shrinks considerably when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Our team handles wrongful death cases and works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on who can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits standing to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. Our team can sort out who qualifies before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines handled with care
items.desc: Families have two years from the date of death, but claims against a government entity carry a much shorter clock. Early guidance helps protect your right to act.

items.title: A full picture of what was lost
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. We work to account for each of these.

items.question: My spouse was killed in a crash on the I-10 through Redlands. Who might be responsible?
items.answer: Responsibility depends on the facts, and it may extend beyond the other driver to an employer, a vehicle manufacturer, or a public agency responsible for the roadway. Because claims involving a city, county, or state agency have a shortened filing period, it helps to speak with an attorney soon. Contact us for a free case review so those possibilities can be reviewed.

items.question: The driver is being charged criminally. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate paths. A criminal case is brought by the state and focuses on punishment; a wrongful death claim is brought by the family and focuses on the losses you carry. The civil claim can move forward regardless of how the criminal matter turns out.

items.question: How much does it cost to contact your team?
items.answer: Nothing. Our team handles wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning no fee is owed unless there is a recovery.
